name: Kakiemon and Imari export porcelain
summary: Japanese export porcelain from Arita. Kakiemon ware has a milk-white body and a spare, asymmetric overglaze design; Imari ware is dense, with blue under the glaze and red and gold over it.

philosophy.core_thesis: A white porcelain can carry two styles of decoration: a spare picture in the open white, and a crowded design in blue, red and gold.
design_principles: Make a milk-white body, called nigoshide, from Arita clay for the Kakiemon type.
Leave large areas of the white body empty and place the design off-centre.
Paint overglaze enamels in red, green, blue, yellow and black, and fire at 800 °C in a muffle kiln.
Use a spare, graceful design of flowering branches, birds, tigers and the quail and millet.
For Imari, paint underglaze blue first, then red and gold over it, so that the surface is full.
Fire the body and the glaze at 1300 °C, and the enamels at 800 °C, in a third firing.
Use lobed edges and brown-edged rims (kuchibeni) on dishes and bowls.
anti_patterns: A centred, symmetrical design in the Kakiemon type
A grey or cloudy porcelain body
Soft shading and realistic depth in the pattern
Painting in blue only with no enamel
Gilding in thick sheet instead of fine lines

form.shape: Octagonal and lobed dishes, bowls, bottles, jars with lids, figures of animals, and tall ceremonial jars.
form.profile: Round or octagonal shapes with a crisp, thin wall; vases have a full belly and a straight neck.
form.foot_and_rim: A neat foot ring with a thin edge, and a rim with a thin brown line (kuchibeni) on Kakiemon dishes.
form.proportion: Dish diameter 20 to 30 cm; vase height 20 to 60 cm; a wall 3 to 6 mm thick.
rules: Make the wall thin and the glaze even and flawless.
Mould lobed or octagonal forms for a dish, for an interesting edge.
Leave up to half of the face of a Kakiemon piece in bare white.
Put the design on one side and let it flow to the rim.

bodies.rule: Use a white, dense porcelain of Izumiyama stone. It must fire to a milk-white that gives a clean ground for the enamels.

methods: slip casting of figures by hand moulds
forming.joins: Lids and handles are luted with slip; figures are moulded in two halves and joined.
forming.details: A brown line on the rim, a flat, even enamel, and a pointed stilt mark under the foot.

glaze.pattern: Kakiemon: a spare flowering branch, a quail and millet, or a tiger, off-centre on white. Imari: dense chrysanthemum, peony and brocade bands in blue, red and gold.
glaze.gloss: Glassy, about 85 to 95 GU, over a clear glaze; the enamels are slightly raised and glossy.
glaze.wear: The enamel can rub off the high places and the gilding can fade; the white body stays clean.

palette.strategy: Kakiemon: a milk-white ground with soft red, green, blue and yellow. Imari: deep underglaze blue with iron red and gold over it.

firing.kiln: A climbing kiln of linked chambers at Arita for the body and glaze, and a small muffle kiln for the enamels.
firing.scale: The Dutch trading company ordered and shipped thousands of pieces from Arita each year after 1659.
firing.signs: A milk-white body, an even flat enamel, a brown rim line and a small stilt mark under the foot.

pieces.form: Octagonal dish with a flowering branch and a brown rim on a milk-white body
Large jar with a lid, dense peony and chrysanthemum bands in blue, red and gold
Tall bottle with a plain milk-white body and a quail and millet in red and green
Lobed bowl with a tiger and bamboo and gold on the rim

positive: milk-white body with a spare asymmetric design
overglaze enamels in red, green and blue

canonical_works.work: Kakiemon dish with quail and millet
Octagonal Kakiemon jar with a lid
Imari jar with peony and brocade

evidence.title: Kakiemon dish with a bird on a rock, about 1670

emotion.target_response: A bright, balanced luxury: the viewer sees clean white and sharp colour and feels the pleasure of a fine cabinet piece.

use_cases: a spare coloured plate on milk-white porcelain
a museum label on Japanese export porcelain
a prompt for a 17th-century collector's cabinet
avoid_when: the brief needs a rustic earthenware look
the brief needs a centred, symmetric design in a single colour

modifiers.how: Change to tin-glazed earthenware and paint a blue version of the motif.
Keep the white porcelain, change the enamels to soft pinks with opaque white, and fill the face with a Chinese garden scene.
